import json, os
from pathlib import Path
modules = json.loads(Path(os.environ['CATALOG']).read_text())['modules']
own = {'greeter', 'hello', 'versioned_3'}
assert own <= {module['name'] for module in modules}
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
hello = next(module for module in modules if module['name'] == 'hello')
pom = Path(os.environ['REPOSITORY']) / 'example/hello' / hello['version'] / ('hello-'+hello['version']+'.pom')
model = ET.parse(pom).getroot()
greeter = next(dep for dep in model.findall('.//{*}dependencies/{*}dependency')
               if dep.findtext('{*}artifactId') == 'greeter')
selected = greeter.findtext('{*}version').strip('[]')
assert '-nix-' in selected
assert (Path(os.environ['REPOSITORY'])/'example/greeter'/selected/('greeter-'+selected+'.jar')).is_file()
for module in modules:
    directory = Path(module['group'].replace('.', '/')) / module['name'] / module['version']
    if module['name'] in own:
        assert '-nix-' in module['version']
    for source in (Path(os.environ['REPOSITORY']) / directory).iterdir():
        if source.suffix in {'.jar', '.pom'}:
            assert (Path(os.environ['RELEASE']) / directory / source.name).read_bytes() == source.read_bytes()

with http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), handler) as server:
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    try:
        base = 'http://127.0.0.1:' + str(server.server_port)
        with open('resources.txt', 'w') as expected:

        for hidden in ('catalog.json', 'nix-support/inputs'):

                try:
                    urllib.request.urlopen(base + '/' + hidden)
                    raise AssertionError('served metadata: ' + hidden)
                except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
                    assert error.code == 404
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        thread.join()

# identity hash codes of its locals, which differ between JVM runs,
# so ahead-of-time compiled classes would differ between builds.

  if clojure "$@" > >(tee "$TMPDIR/clojure.log") 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi
  if grep -qE 'could not be resolved|Could not transfer|Could not find artifact|Failed to read artifact descriptor|Unable to clone|Network is unreachable' "$TMPDIR/clojure.log"; then

  fi
  return 1
}

stale

opam install --ignore-pin-depends ./hello.opam
# The tests run once every package of the project is installed.
# A test of one package often uses another package of the same
# project without declaring it, which a dune build at the
# project root never notices.
opam reinstall --ignore-pin-depends --with-test hello

# lock run records as the outputs.
mkdir -p "$out/nix-support/opam-purifier-files"
opam show --list-files hello > "$out/nix-support/opam-purifier-files/"hello

# this switch installed, which `opam-purifier update` writes into

(cd "$out/nix-support/opam-locked" && opam lock hello > /dev/null)

link() {
  # $1 publication, $2 key, $3 the artifact's directory, $4 its
  # file name after "<artifactId>-<version>", and $5 "optional"
  # for a file the build may leave out.
  local dir=$3 version
  version=$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf '%f\n' | head -n 1)

  if [ ! -f "$file" ] && [ "${5:-}" = optional ]; then

  fi
  mkdir -p "$maven/nix-support/artifacts/$1"

}

while IFS=$'\t' read -r rel url target; do
  mkdir -p "$out/$(dirname "$rel")"
  ln -s "$target" "$out/$rel"
done < "$checkoutsPath"

count=$(jq length "$reposPath")
for ((i = 0; i < count; i++)); do
  repo() { jq -r --argjson i "$i" ".[\$i]$1" "$reposPath"; }
  rel=$(repo .path)
  url=$(repo .url)
  bare="$out/$rel"
  git init --quiet --bare "$bare"

  # The trees of the checkouts of this repository.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r _ checkoutUrl target; do
    [ "$checkoutUrl" = "$url" ] || continue
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TMPDIR/index" git --git-dir="$bare" --work-tree="$target" \
      -c core.autocrlf=false add --all --force .
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TMPDIR/index" git --git-dir="$bare" write-tree >/dev/null
    rm -f "$TMPDIR/index"
  done < "$checkoutsPath"

  commits=$(jq --argjson i "$i" '.[$i].commits | length' "$reposPath")
  for ((c = 0; c < commits; c++)); do
    want=$(jq -r --argjson i "$i" --argjson c "$c" '.[$i].commits[$c].sha' "$reposPath")
    got=$(jq -j --argjson i "$i" --argjson c "$c" '.[$i].commits[$c].object' "$reposPath" |
      git --git-dir="$bare" hash-object -t commit -w --stdin)
    if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
      echo "clojure-cli-purifier: the recorded commit $want of $url rebuilt as $got" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  repo '.shallow[]' >"$bare/shallow"
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r tag sha; do
    git --git-dir="$bare" update-ref "refs/tags/$tag" "$sha"
  done < <(repo '.tags | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value)"')

  # Every checkout must rebuild the tree its commit names. A checkout
  # whose files differ from that tree, such as one changed by a git
  # attribute, would leave the commit without its tree.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r rel2 checkoutUrl _; do
    [ "$checkoutUrl" = "$url" ] || continue
    sha=$(basename "$rel2")
    if ! git --git-dir="$bare" cat-file -e "$sha^{tree}" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "clojure-cli-purifier: the checkout of $url at $sha does not rebuild the tree of its commit" >&2
      exit 1
    fi

deno() {
  local status=0
  command deno "$@" 2> >(tee -a "$TMPDIR/deno-errors" >&2) || status=$?

  return "$status"

cat >tiny/Cargo.toml <<'EOF'

edition = "2021"

license = "MIT"
EOF

(cd tiny && cargo package --offline --quiet)

cp tiny/target/package/tiny-0.1.0.crate www/dl/ti/ny/

printf '{"dl":"%s","api":"http://127.0.0.1:%s"}\n' "$dl" "$port" >index/config.json

git -C index add -A

cat >gitdep/Cargo.toml <<'EOF'
[package]
name = "gitdep"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
EOF

[package]
name = "app"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]

gitdep = { git = "file://$PWD/gitdep" }

# opam records the modification time of every file it installs in
# <package>.changes. Nix sets the time of each file in the store to

  local status=0
  command deno "$@" 2> >(tee -a "$TMPDIR/deno-errors" >&2) || status=$?

}

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# The functions of the clojure-cli-purifier command that read and write
# files without running the Clojure CLI. The package puts them before the
# command, and the unit tests (tests/unit.sh) source them on their own.

# A path of the project directory, relative to the source root.
inProject() {
  local projectDir=$1 file=$2
  if [ "$projectDir" = . ]; then echo "$file"; else echo "$projectDir/$file"; fi
}

# The files that decide what the project resolves, relative to the source
# root: the deps.edn and build.clj of the project, and the deps.edn of
# every other directory of the source root, which a local dependency may
# be.
definitionFiles() {
  local sourceRoot=$1 projectDir=$2 depsEdn
  depsEdn=$(inProject "$projectDir" deps.edn)
  echo "$depsEdn"
  if [ -f "$sourceRoot/$(inProject "$projectDir" build.clj)" ]; then inProject "$projectDir" build.clj; fi
  (
    cd "$sourceRoot" || exit
    find . \( -name target -o -name .cpcache -o -name .git -o -name node_modules \) -prune \
      -o -name deps.edn -type f -printf '%P\n' | grep -vxF "$depsEdn" | LC_ALL=C sort || true
  )
}

# The SHA-256 of the given files of the source root, in that order, in
# hex. The Nix builder hashes the same files in the same order.
definitionHash() {
  local sourceRoot=$1 file
  shift
  for file in "$@"; do
    if [ -f "$sourceRoot/$file" ]; then cat "$sourceRoot/$file"; fi
  done | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
}

# The directory of the project relative to its source root, as the
# lockfile records it.
# The content hash of a lockfile: the SHA-256 of the lockfile without its
# contentHash field, as JSON with sorted keys and no spaces. The function
# builtins.toJSON writes the same text, so read-lock.nix computes the same
# hash.
contentHash() {
  jq -S -c 'del(.contentHash)' "$1" | tr -d '\n' | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
}

lockProjectDir() {
  jq -r '.projectDir // "."' "$1"
}

# The source root of a project root, by the project directory the lockfile
# records.
sourceRootOf() {
  local root=$1 projectDir=$2
  if [ "$projectDir" = . ]; then echo "$root"; else echo "${root%/"$projectDir"}"; fi
}

# Writes settings.xml for the lock run. A settings.xml of the user brings
# its proxies, mirrors and repository credentials. Without one, the proxy
# of https_proxy applies, because Maven Resolver reads no proxy from the
# environment.
writeSettings() {
  local m2=$1 realHome=$2 proxy rest auth hostport host port user pass
  mkdir -p "$m2"
  if [ -f "$realHome/.m2/settings.xml" ]; then
    cp "$realHome/.m2/settings.xml" "$m2/settings.xml"
    return
  fi
  proxy=${https_proxy:-${HTTPS_PROXY:-}}
  [ -n "$proxy" ] || return 0
  rest=${proxy#*://}
  auth=
  if [[ $rest == *@* ]]; then
    auth=${rest%%@*}
    rest=${rest#*@}
  fi
  hostport=${rest%%/*}
  host=${hostport%%:*}
  port=${hostport##*:}
  if [ "$port" = "$hostport" ]; then port=80; fi
  user=${auth%%:*}
  pass=${auth#*:}
  {
    echo '<settings>'
    echo '<proxies><proxy><id>environment</id><active>true</active>'
    echo "<protocol>http</protocol><host>$host</host><port>$port</port>"
    if [ -n "$auth" ]; then echo "<username>$user</username><password>$pass</password>"; fi
    echo '<nonProxyHosts>localhost|127.0.0.1</nonProxyHosts></proxy></proxies>'
    echo '</settings>'
  } >"$m2/settings.xml"
}

# Adds a mirror to a settings.xml for each "<id>=<url>" given: the mirror
# serves the repository of that id, from that URL. A file that does not
# exist yet becomes a settings.xml with only the mirrors.
addMirrors() {
  local settings=$1 spec block=""
  shift
  [ $# -gt 0 ] || return 0
  for spec in "$@"; do
    block="$block<mirror>
<id>purifier-${spec%%=*}</id>
<mirrorOf>${spec%%=*}</mirrorOf>
<url>${spec#*=}</url>
</mirror>
"
  done
  if [ ! -f "$settings" ]; then
    printf '<settings>\n</settings>\n' >"$settings"
  fi
  if grep -q '<mirrors>' "$settings"; then
    awk -v block="$block" '!done && sub(/<mirrors>/, "<mirrors>\n" block) { done = 1 } { print }' \
      "$settings" >"$settings.tmp"
  else
    awk -v block="$block" '!done && sub(/<\/settings>/, "<mirrors>\n" block "</mirrors>\n</settings>") { done = 1 } { print }' \
      "$settings" >"$settings.tmp"
  fi
  mv "$settings.tmp" "$settings"
}

# Prints "<id>\t<url>\t<mirrorOf>" for each mirror of a settings.xml.
# Writes the repository metadata a lockfile recorded into a local
# repository, so that a lock run resolves each version range and SNAPSHOT
# to the version the lockfile holds. The lockfile names each version list
# after its repository, and a lock run through a mirror reads it under the
# id of the mirror. Metadata under the directory prefixes after the
# settings file is left out, so the lock run resolves those libraries
# anew.
seedMetadata() {
  local lockFile=$1 m2=$2 settings=$3 id of path contents prefix skip
  shift 3
  local -a renames=(-e 's/^/&/')
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id _ of; do
    if [ -n "$of" ] && [[ $of != *[*,!]* ]]; then
      renames+=(-e "s/maven-metadata-$of\\.xml/maven-metadata-$id.xml/g")
    fi
  done < <(mirrors "$settings")
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r path contents; do
    skip=0
    for prefix in "$@"; do
      if [[ $path == "$prefix"* ]]; then skip=1; fi
    done
    [ $skip = 0 ] || continue
    path="$(dirname "$path")/$(basename "$path" | sed "${renames[@]}")"
    mkdir -p "$m2/$(dirname "$path")"
    printf '%s' "$contents" | base64 -d | sed "${renames[@]}" >"$m2/$path"
  done < <(jq -r '.metadata[] | [.path, (.contents | @base64)] | @tsv' "$lockFile")
}

mirrors() {
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
  awk '
    /<mirror>/ { inside = 1; id = ""; url = ""; of = "" }
    inside && /<id>/ { id = $0; gsub(/.*<id>|<\/id>.*/, "", id) }
    inside && /<url>/ { url = $0; gsub(/.*<url>|<\/url>.*/, "", url) }
    inside && /<mirrorOf>/ { of = $0; gsub(/.*<mirrorOf>|<\/mirrorOf>.*/, "", of) }
    /<\/mirror>/ { print id "\t" url "\t" of; inside = 0 }
  ' "$1"
}

# Prints the id of the repository a file of a local repository directory
# came from, as its _remote.repositories file records it, or nothing.
remoteId() {
  awk -F'>' -v file="$2" '$1 == file { sub(/=$/, "", $2); print $2; exit }' \
    "$1/_remote.repositories" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Prints a JSON list of command lines, each a list of words, from command
# lines given as strings. Each splits into words the way the shell splits
# an unquoted word.
commandsJson() {
  local line
  local -a words
  for line in "$@"; do
    read -ra words <<<"$line"
    printf '%s\n' "${words[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -sc .
  done | jq -sc .
}
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# clojure-cli-purifier: locks the downloads of a deps.edn project,
# prefetches them for the Clojure CLI, and publishes what Nix built.
#
# The package sets PURIFIER_LIB (the Nix library, nix/lib), PURIFIER_FORMAT
# (the lock format version it reads), PURIFIER_HELPER (helper.clj),
# PURIFIER_TOOLS_JAR (the tools jar of the Clojure CLI, which runs the
# helper), PURIFIER_NIXPKGS (the nixpkgs source the package was built from),
# PURIFIER_SHARED_REF (the flake reference of the shared purifier library)
# and JAVA_CMD (the JVM of the Clojure CLI).

lockName=clojure-cli-purifier.lock.json
# What `update` re-resolves: every library, or the libraries whose metadata
# lies under these directories of the local repository.
updateAll=0
updatePrefixes=()

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  clojure-cli-purifier lock [--lockfile PATH] [--force] [--build ARGS]... [--test ARGS]...
                            [--alias :NAME]... [--user-aliases]
                            [--source DIR] [--mirror ID=URL]...
      Runs the project with an empty local Maven repository and an empty
      gitlibs directory, and records every file the Clojure CLI downloads,
      the outputs of the build commands and the commands themselves in
      clojure-cli-purifier.lock.json.

      --build ARGS   A Clojure CLI command line the Nix build runs, such as
                     "-T:build uber". It may repeat. The default is the
                     uber or jar function of build.clj, when there is one
                     and deps.edn has a :build alias.
      --test ARGS    A Clojure CLI command line the Nix build runs when its
                     checks are on, such as "-M:test". It may repeat.
      --alias :NAME  An alias to prepare. The default is every alias of
                     deps.edn. It may repeat.
      --user-aliases Also prepares the aliases of the user deps.edn, for
                     the interactive mode. The Nix build ignores them.
                     --no-user-aliases stops preparing them.
      --source DIR   The directory that holds the project and the local
                     dependencies outside it, such as the root of a
                     repository with several projects. The Nix build takes
                     it as src. The default is the project root.
      --mirror ID=URL
                     Downloads the files of the repository ID, such as
                     central, from a mirror at URL during the lock run.
                     The lockfile names each such file by its URL in the
                     repository, with the mirror as a fallback. It may
                     repeat.

      Each option replaces its part of an existing lockfile, and a relock
      keeps every part no option names. Without options or --force, an
      up-to-date lockfile is left as it is. A relock keeps the versions
      the lockfile resolved its version ranges and SNAPSHOTs to.
  clojure-cli-purifier update [--lockfile PATH] [--mirror ID=URL]... [LIB]...
      Relocks the project and resolves the version ranges and SNAPSHOTs of
      every library anew, or those of the named libraries, such as
      org.clojure/core.memoize. Versions that deps.edn names exactly change
      only when deps.edn does.
  clojure-cli-purifier prefetch [--lockfile PATH]
      Builds the locked downloads into the Nix store, keeps them alive with
      a GC root in .clojure-cli-purifier beside the lockfile, and links
      .clojure-cli-purifier/bin/clojure. With that directory first on PATH,
      `clojure` runs on the locked downloads alone, with no network.
  clojure-cli-purifier publish [--lockfile PATH] [--repository ID=URL] [--dry-run]
      Builds the release of the project with Nix and deploys its jar and
      POM, without compiling anything outside the sandbox. The default
      repository is Clojars, with CLOJARS_USERNAME and CLOJARS_PASSWORD.
      Another repository takes its credentials from the server of the same
      id in ~/.m2/settings.xml.

  Every command takes --lockfile PATH, for a lockfile kept outside the
  project. The environment variable CLOJURE_CLI_PURIFIER_LOCKFILE gives the
  same path, and --lockfile takes precedence over it. The default is
  clojure-cli-purifier.lock.json in the project root.
EOF
}

die() {
  echo "clojure-cli-purifier: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

# The project root: the nearest directory, from here upwards, that holds
# deps.edn.
projectRoot() {
  local dir
  dir=$(pwd)
  while [ "$dir" != / ]; do
    if [ -f "$dir/deps.edn" ]; then
      echo "$dir"
      return
    fi
    dir=$(dirname "$dir")
  done
  die "no deps.edn in $(pwd) or above it"
}

clojureVersion() {
  clojure --version | sed -n 's/^Clojure CLI version //p'
}

javaVersion() {
  "$JAVA_CMD" -XshowSettings:properties -version 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^ *java.version = //p'
}

helper() {
  "$JAVA_CMD" -cp "$PURIFIER_TOOLS_JAR" clojure.main "$PURIFIER_HELPER" "$@"
}

# The lockfile of the project at root: the path given to --lockfile, then
# the path in CLOJURE_CLI_PURIFIER_LOCKFILE, then clojure-cli-purifier.lock.json
# in the project root. It prints an absolute path.
lockFileOf() {
  local root=$1 given=$2 path
  path=${given:-${CLOJURE_CLI_PURIFIER_LOCKFILE:-$root/$lockName}}
  case $path in
  /*) echo "$path" ;;
  *) echo "$(pwd)/$path" ;;
  esac
}

# Prints why the lockfile does not fit the project at root, with the
# command that fixes it, or nothing when the lockfile was made from this
# project definition, by this lock format and with this Clojure CLI.
lockProblem() {
  local root=$1 lockFile=$2 files sourceRoot
  if [ ! -f "$lockFile" ]; then
    echo "$lockFile does not exist; run clojure-cli-purifier lock"
    return
  fi
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$lockFile" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$lockFile is not a JSON object, so it is not a clojure-cli-purifier lockfile; run clojure-cli-purifier lock --force"
    return
  fi
  if [ "$(jq -r .version "$lockFile")" != "$PURIFIER_FORMAT" ]; then
    echo "$lockFile has lock format version $(jq -r .version "$lockFile"), and this clojure-cli-purifier reads version $PURIFIER_FORMAT; run clojure-cli-purifier lock --force"
    return
  fi
  if [ "$(jq -r .contentHash "$lockFile")" != "$(contentHash "$lockFile")" ]; then
    echo "$lockFile does not match its contentHash, so it was edited after the lock run; run clojure-cli-purifier lock --force"
    return
  fi
  sourceRoot=$(sourceRootOf "$root" "$(lockProjectDir "$lockFile")")
  mapfile -t files < <(jq -r '.definitionFiles[]' "$lockFile")
  if [ "$(jq -r .definitionHash "$lockFile")" != "$(definitionHash "$sourceRoot" "${files[@]}")" ]; then
    echo "the project definition in $sourceRoot ($(jq -r '.definitionFiles | join(", ")' "$lockFile")) changed after $lockFile was made; run clojure-cli-purifier lock"
    return
  fi
  if [ "$(jq -r .clojureVersion "$lockFile")" != "$(clojureVersion)" ]; then
    echo "$lockFile was made with Clojure CLI $(jq -r .clojureVersion "$lockFile"), and this clojure-cli-purifier runs Clojure CLI $(clojureVersion); run clojure-cli-purifier lock"
  fi
}

lockIsCurrent() {
  [ -z "$(lockProblem "$1" "$2")" ]
}

# Preserve the caller's -Sdeps and execution mode while activating the
# selected coordinates for CLI resolution. Independent bases use private
# repository aliases prepared below.
clojure() {
  if [ -z "${PURIFIER_PROVIDED_CONFIG:-}" ]; then command clojure "$@"; return; fi
  local supplied='' mode=0 configuration
  local arguments=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
    -Sdeps)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "-Sdeps needs an EDN map"
      supplied=$2; shift 2 ;;
    -T?*)
      if [[ $1 == -T:* ]]; then
        arguments+=("$1:nix-purifier-project-inputs")
      else
        # -Ttool names an installed tool, rather than project aliases.
        # Its independent basis reads the prepared private Maven aliases.
        arguments+=("$1")
      fi
      shift
      arguments+=("$@")
      mode=1
      break ;;
    -M* | -X* | -T | -A*)
      arguments+=("$1:nix-purifier-project-inputs")
      shift
      arguments+=("$@")
      mode=1
      break ;;
    *) arguments+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
  done
  if [ "$mode" = 0 ]; then arguments=(-A:nix-purifier-project-inputs "${arguments[@]}"); fi
  configuration=$(helper merge-input-config "$PURIFIER_PROVIDED_CONFIG" "$supplied")
  command clojure -Sdeps "$configuration" "${arguments[@]}"
}

stageInputAliases() {
  local repository=$1 metadata=$2
  shift 2
  local definitions=()
  mapfile -t definitions < <(find "$@" \( -name target -o -name .git -o -name _repos -o -name .cpcache -o -name .clojure-cli-purifier \) -prune \
    -o -type f -name deps.edn -print)
  helper mvn-requests "${definitions[@]}" > "$metadata/requests.tsv"
  python3 "$PURIFIER_LIB/maven-aliases.py" "$PURIFIER_PROJECT_INPUTS_TOOLS" \
    "$repository" "$metadata" "$metadata/requests.tsv"
}

cmdLock() {
  local force=0 userAliases="" source="" lockArg=""
  local -a builds=() tests=() aliases=() mirrorSpecs=() inputArgs=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
    --force) force=1 ;;
    --input)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "lock: --input takes a flake package"
      inputArgs+=(--input "$2")
      force=1
      shift
      ;;
    --lockfile)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "lock: --lockfile takes a path"
      lockArg=$2
      shift
      ;;
    --build)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "lock: --build takes a command line"
      builds+=("$2")
      shift
      ;;
    --test)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "lock: --test takes a command line"
      tests+=("$2")
      shift
      ;;
    --alias)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "lock: --alias takes an alias"
      aliases+=("$2")
      shift
      ;;
    --user-aliases) userAliases=true ;;
    --no-user-aliases) userAliases=false ;;
    --mirror)
      if [ $# -lt 2 ] || [[ $2 != *=* ]]; then die "lock: --mirror takes ID=URL"; fi
      mirrorSpecs+=("$2")
      shift
      ;;
    --source)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "lock: --source takes a directory"
      source=$2
      shift
      ;;
    *) die "lock: unknown argument $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
  done

  local root lockFile
  root=$(projectRoot)
  lockFile=$(lockFileOf "$root" "$lockArg")
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$lockFile")"
  # A relock starts from a valid lockfile only.
  if [ -f "$lockFile" ] && ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$lockFile" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ $force = 1 ] || die "$lockFile is not a JSON object; run clojure-cli-purifier lock --force"
    rm "$lockFile"
  fi
  local explicit=0
  if [ ${#builds[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ ${#tests[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ ${#aliases[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ -n "$userAliases" ] || [ -n "$source" ]; then
    explicit=1
  fi

  # The source root holds the project and its local dependencies. A relock
  # without --source keeps the source root of the existing lockfile.
  local sourceRoot projectDir
  if [ -n "$source" ]; then
    sourceRoot=$(cd "$source" && pwd)
  elif [ -f "$lockFile" ]; then
    sourceRoot=$(sourceRootOf "$root" "$(lockProjectDir "$lockFile")")
  else
    sourceRoot=$root
  fi
  case $root in
  "$sourceRoot") projectDir=. ;;
  "$sourceRoot"/*) projectDir=${root#"$sourceRoot/"} ;;
  *) die "lock: the project $root is not inside the source root $sourceRoot" ;;
  esac
  if [ $force = 0 ] && [ $explicit = 0 ] && lockIsCurrent "$root" "$lockFile"; then
    echo "clojure-cli-purifier: $lockFile is up to date"
    return
  fi

  # Each option replaces its part of the existing lockfile, and a part no
  # option names keeps its value from the lockfile.
  local buildJson testJson aliasJson
  local hasLock=0
  if [ -f "$lockFile" ]; then hasLock=1; fi
  if [ ${#builds[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    buildJson=$(commandsJson "${builds[@]}")
  elif [ $hasLock = 1 ]; then
    buildJson=$(jq -c .build "$lockFile")
  else
    # The default build runs build.clj through the :build alias of deps.edn.
    # A project whose build.clj runs under babashka has no :build alias.
    if [ -f "$root/build.clj" ] && helper aliases "$root/deps.edn" | grep -qx ':build'; then
      if grep -q '(defn uber\b' "$root/build.clj"; then
        builds=("-T:build uber")
      elif grep -q '(defn jar\b' "$root/build.clj"; then
        builds=("-T:build jar")
      fi
    fi
    buildJson=$(commandsJson "${builds[@]}")
  fi
  if [ ${#tests[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    testJson=$(commandsJson "${tests[@]}")
  elif [ $hasLock = 1 ]; then
    testJson=$(jq -c .test "$lockFile")
  else
    testJson='[]'
  fi
  if [ ${#aliases[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    aliasJson=$(printf '%s\n' "${aliases[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
  elif [ $hasLock = 1 ]; then
    aliasJson=$(jq -c .aliases "$lockFile")
  else
    aliasJson=null
  fi
  if [ -z "$userAliases" ]; then
    if [ $hasLock = 1 ]; then userAliases=$(jq -r .userAliases "$lockFile"); else userAliases=false; fi
  fi

  local work
  work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/clojure-cli-purifier.XXXXXX")
  # Git names the repository of a checkout by its physical path, which the
  # lock run matches against the gitlibs directory below. On macOS the
  # temporary directory lies behind the /var symlink.
  work=$(cd "$work" && pwd -P)
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064 # work is fixed from here on
  trap "chmod -R u+w '$work' 2>/dev/null; rm -rf '$work'" EXIT
  mkdir -p "$work/source" "$work/home" "$work/config" "$work/cache" "$work/gitlibs" "$work/java-tmp"
  tar -C "$sourceRoot" --exclude=target --exclude=.cpcache --exclude=.clojure-cli-purifier --exclude=.git -cf - . | tar -C "$work/source" -xf -
  local project="$work/source"
  if [ "$projectDir" != . ]; then project="$work/source/$projectDir"; fi

  # The lock run sees what a sandboxed build sees: an empty local
  # repository, an empty gitlibs directory and no user configuration. The
  # JVMs take their local repository from user.home, which HOME does not
  # set.
  local realHome=$HOME userConfig
  userConfig="${CLJ_CONFIG:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$realHome/.config}/clojure}"
  if [ -z "${CLJ_CONFIG:-}" ] && [ ! -d "$userConfig" ]; then userConfig="$realHome/.clojure"; fi
  writeSettings "$work/home/.m2" "$realHome"
  addMirrors "$work/home/.m2/settings.xml" "${mirrorSpecs[@]}"
  # A lock keeps the versions the lockfile resolved its version ranges and
  # SNAPSHOTs to, from the metadata it recorded. `update` leaves out the
  # metadata of the libraries it updates.
  if [ $hasLock = 1 ] && [ "$updateAll" = 0 ]; then
    mkdir -p "$work/home/.m2/repository"
    seedMetadata "$lockFile" "$work/home/.m2/repository" "$work/home/.m2/settings.xml" "${updatePrefixes[@]}"
  fi
  local previousArgs=() refreshArgs=()
  if [ "$hasLock" = 1 ]; then previousArgs=(--previous "$lockFile"); fi
  if [ "$updateAll" = 1 ]; then refreshArgs=(--refresh); fi
  python3 "$PURIFIER_PROJECT_INPUTS_TOOLS/project_inputs.py" pin "${previousArgs[@]}" \
    "${inputArgs[@]}" "${refreshArgs[@]}" --output "$work/inputs.json"
  if [ "$(jq length "$work/inputs.json")" -gt 0 ]; then
    python3 "$PURIFIER_PROJECT_INPUTS_TOOLS/project_inputs.py" maven --inputs "$work/inputs.json" \
      --destination "$work/home/.m2/repository" --metadata "$work/input-metadata" --roots "$work/inputs"
    export PURIFIER_PROVIDED_CONFIG="$work/input-metadata/project-inputs.edn"
    stageInputAliases "$work/home/.m2/repository" "$work/input-metadata" "$work/source" "$work/gitlibs"
  fi
  echo '{}' >"$work/config/deps.edn"
  export HOME="$work/home"
  export CLJ_CONFIG="$work/config"
  export CLJ_CACHE="$work/cache"
  export GITLIBS="$work/gitlibs"
  export CLJ_JVM_OPTS="-Duser.home=$HOME -Djava.io.tmpdir=$work/java-tmp"
  export JAVA_OPTS="$CLJ_JVM_OPTS"
  export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
  local m2="$work/home/.m2/repository"

  # The aliases to prepare: the given ones, or every alias of the project.
  local -a prepare
  if [ "$aliasJson" = null ]; then
    mapfile -t prepare < <(helper aliases "$project/deps.edn")
  else
    mapfile -t prepare < <(jq -r '.[]' <<<"$aliasJson")
  fi
  local -a userPrepare=()
  if [ "$userAliases" = true ] && [ -f "$userConfig/deps.edn" ]; then
    mapfile -t userPrepare < <(helper aliases "$userConfig/deps.edn")
  fi

  echo "clojure-cli-purifier: locking $root"
  # Each step runs in a subshell whose output goes to the log, and the
  # caller tests its status with ||, which turns off errexit inside it. So
  # every command in a step exits the step itself when it fails.
  local alias log="$work/log"
  : >"$log"
  # Runs the Clojure CLI to resolve and download. A git dependency that
  # needs preparing stops the CLI with "must be prepared before use" once
  # it has resolved the project and cloned the dependency. That is no
  # failure of the first pass, which has to record the checkouts before
  # they are prepared. It makes the lock run resolve once more after the
  # preparation.
  resolveWith() {
    local output status=0
    output=$(clojure "$@" 2>&1) || status=$?
    printf '%s\n' "$output"
    if [ $status != 0 ]; then
      if grep -q 'must be prepared before use' <<<"$output"; then
        touch "$work/needs-prep"
      else
        return 1
      fi
    fi
  }
  # A POM can choose dependencies by architecture, through a profile that
  # Maven Resolver activates from os.arch. The project resolves again for
  # each architecture the flake builds for, so the lock holds what every
  # one of them resolves.
  local thisArch
  thisArch=$("$JAVA_CMD" -XshowSettings:properties -version 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^ *os.arch = //p')
  resolveProject() {
    local otherArch archOpts
    (
      cd "$project" || exit 1
      resolveWith -P || exit 1
      for alias in "${prepare[@]}"; do
        resolveWith -P "-M$alias" || exit 1
      done
    ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log" || die "preparing the project failed; see the output above"
    for otherArch in amd64 aarch64; do
      [ "$otherArch" != "$thisArch" ] || continue
      archOpts="$CLJ_JVM_OPTS -Dos.arch=$otherArch"
      (
        cd "$project" || exit 1
        CLJ_JVM_OPTS=$archOpts resolveWith -Sforce -P || exit 1
        for alias in "${prepare[@]}"; do
          CLJ_JVM_OPTS=$archOpts resolveWith -Sforce -P "-M$alias" || exit 1
        done
      ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log" || die "preparing the project for $otherArch failed; see the output above"
    done
  }
  resolveProject
  if [ ${#userPrepare[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    # The aliases of the user deps.edn resolve with it, in a cache of their
    # own.
    (
      cd "$project" || exit 1
      export CLJ_CONFIG="$work/user-config"
      mkdir -p "$CLJ_CONFIG"
      cp "$userConfig/deps.edn" "$CLJ_CONFIG/deps.edn"
      for alias in "${userPrepare[@]}"; do
        CLJ_CACHE="$work/user-cache" clojure -Sforce -P "-M$alias" || exit 1
      done
    ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log" || die "preparing the user aliases failed; see the output above"
  fi

  # The git dependencies, before preparing them changes their checkouts.
  local gitEntries="$work/git.jsonl" gitRepos="$work/repos.jsonl"
  : >"$gitEntries"
  : >"$gitRepos"
  local bare url checkout rev rel copy hash tree index="$work/index"
  local -a revs commits parents
  while IFS= read -r bare; do
    url=$(git --git-dir="$bare" config remote.origin.url)
    revs=()
    for checkout in "$GITLIBS"/libs/*/*/*; do
      [ -f "$checkout/.git" ] || continue
      case $(sed -n 's/^gitdir: //p' "$checkout/.git") in
      "$bare"/*) ;;
      *) continue ;;
      esac
      rev=$(basename "$checkout")
      revs+=("$rev")
      rel=${checkout#"$GITLIBS/"}
      copy="$work/checkout"
      rm -rf "$copy"
      mkdir -p "$copy"
      tar -C "$checkout" --exclude=./.git -cf - . | tar -C "$copy" -xf -
      hash=$(nix-hash --type sha256 --sri "$copy")
      # The Nix build rebuilds the commit from the files of the checkout,
      # so the files must give the tree of the commit.
      tree=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$index" git --git-dir="$bare" --work-tree="$copy" -c core.autocrlf=false add --all --force . &&
        GIT_INDEX_FILE="$index" git --git-dir="$bare" write-tree)
      rm -f "$index"
      if [ "$tree" != "$(git --git-dir="$bare" rev-parse "$rev^{tree}")" ]; then
        die "the checkout of $url at $rev does not give the tree of its commit, so the Nix build could not rebuild the commit"
      fi
      jq -cn --arg path "$rel" --arg url "$url" --arg rev "$rev" --arg hash "$hash" \
        '{ path: $path, git: { url: $url, rev: $rev, submodules: false, leaveDotGit: false, commitObject: null }, hash: $hash }' >>"$gitEntries"
    done
    [ ${#revs[@]} -gt 0 ] || continue
    # The commits the Clojure CLI may read: the locked ones, and when one
    # repository has several, every commit between them and their merge
    # base, which an ancestry check walks. A commit with a parent outside
    # that set is a shallow boundary.
    if [ ${#revs[@]} = 1 ]; then
      commits=("${revs[0]}")
    else
      local base
      base=$(git --git-dir="$bare" merge-base --octopus "${revs[@]}")
      mapfile -t parents < <(git --git-dir="$bare" rev-parse "$base^@")
      mapfile -t commits < <(git --git-dir="$bare" rev-list "${revs[@]}" --not "${parents[@]}")
    fi
    local commitJson shallowJson tagJson c p
    commitJson=$(for c in "${commits[@]}"; do
      git --git-dir="$bare" cat-file commit "$c" | jq -Rs --arg sha "$c" '{ sha: $sha, object: . }'
    done | jq -sc .)
    shallowJson=$(for c in "${commits[@]}"; do
      read -ra parents < <(git --git-dir="$bare" rev-list --parents -n1 "$c" | cut -s -d' ' -f2-)
      if [ ${#parents[@]} = 0 ]; then
        continue
      fi
      for p in "${parents[@]}"; do
        if ! printf '%s\n' "${commits[@]}" | grep -qx "$p"; then
          echo "$c"
          break
        fi
      done
    done | LC_ALL=C sort -u | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
    tagJson=$(for c in "${revs[@]}"; do
      git --git-dir="$bare" tag --points-at "$c" | jq -R --arg rev "$c" '{ key: ., value: $rev }'
    done | jq -sc 'from_entries')
    jq -cn --arg path "${bare#"$GITLIBS/"}" --arg url "$url" \
      --argjson commits "$commitJson" --argjson shallow "$shallowJson" --argjson tags "$tagJson" \
      '{ path: $path, url: $url, commits: $commits, shallow: $shallow, tags: $tags }' >>"$gitRepos"
  done < <(find "$GITLIBS/_repos" -name HEAD -not -path '*/worktrees/*' -printf '%h\n' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)

  if [ -n "${PURIFIER_PROVIDED_CONFIG:-}" ]; then
    stageInputAliases "$m2" "$work/input-metadata" "$work/source" "$GITLIBS"
  fi

  # Git dependencies that need preparing, then the build and its tests.
  local stamp="$work/stamp"
  touch "$stamp"
  sleep 1
  (
    cd "$project" || exit 1
    clojure -X:deps prep :aliases "[${prepare[*]}]" || exit 1
  ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log" || die "preparing the git dependencies failed; see the output above"
  # The passes that the missing preparation cut short run again.
  if [ -f "$work/needs-prep" ]; then
    resolveProject
  fi
  (
    cd "$project" || exit 1
    while IFS= read -r command; do
      mapfile -t words < <(jq -r '.[]' <<<"$command")
      echo "clojure-cli-purifier: clojure ${words[*]}"
      clojure "${words[@]}" || exit 1
    done < <(jq -c '.[]' <<<"$buildJson" && jq -c '.[]' <<<"$testJson")
  ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log" || die "the build failed; see the output above"

  # The outputs: the jars the build commands created.
  local outputs="$work/outputs.jsonl" output mainClass
  : >"$outputs"
  while IFS= read -r output; do
    mainClass=$(unzip -p "$project/$output" META-INF/MANIFEST.MF 2>/dev/null |
      tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^Main-Class: *//p' | jq -R . | jq -s 'first // null')
    jq -cn --arg path "$output" --argjson mainClass "$mainClass" '{ path: $path, mainClass: $mainClass }' >>"$outputs"
  done < <(cd "$project" && find . \( -name .cpcache -o -name classes \) -prune -o \
    \( -name '*.jar' -o -name '*.war' \) -type f -newer "$stamp" -printf '%P\n' | LC_ALL=C sort)

  # The project: from the POM the build wrote, or the directory name.
  local pom=null group="" name version=null pomPath pomFile
  name=$(basename "$root")
  pomPath=$(cd "$project" && find . -name .cpcache -prune -o -name pom.xml -type f -newer "$stamp" -printf '%P\n' | LC_ALL=C sort | head -1)
  if [ -n "$pomPath" ]; then
    pom=$(jq -n --arg p "$pomPath" '$p')
    pomFile="$project/$pomPath"
    pomField() {
      awk -v tag="$1" '
        /<parent>/ { p = 1 }
        /<\/parent>/ { p = 0; next }
        !p && index($0, "<" tag ">") { gsub(".*<" tag ">|</" tag ">.*", ""); print; exit }
      ' "$pomFile"
    }
    group=$(pomField groupId)
    name=$(pomField artifactId)
    version=$(pomField version | jq -R . | jq -s 'first // null')
  fi

  # The repositories the downloads came from, by the id Maven Resolver
  # records: those of every basis the Clojure CLI wrote, and the mirrors of
  # settings.xml.
  declare -A repositoryUrl mirrorOf
  local id of
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r id url of; do
    if [[ $url != */ ]]; then url="$url/"; fi
    repositoryUrl[$id]=$url
    if [ -n "$of" ]; then mirrorOf[$id]=$of; fi
  done < <(
    mapfile -t bases < <(find "$project/.cpcache" "$work/cache" "$work/user-cache" -name '*.basis' 2>/dev/null)
    if [ ${#bases[@]} -gt 0 ]; then helper repos "${bases[@]}"; fi
    mirrors "$work/home/.m2/settings.xml"
  )

  # Every file in the local repository is a download, except the records
  # Maven Resolver keeps. Version lists change on the server, so they are
  # kept with their contents. The rest is named in the _remote.repositories
  # file of its directory, with the id of the repository it came from.
  local artifacts="$work/artifacts.jsonl" metadata="$work/metadata.jsonl"
  local -a untracked=() unknown=()
  : >"$artifacts"
  : >"$metadata"
  # The resolver names the version list of a repository after its id. The
  # build resolves without the mirrors of the lock run, so a version list a
  # mirror of one repository served takes the id of that repository.
  local -a renames=(-e 's/^/&/')
  local mirrorId
  for mirrorId in "${!mirrorOf[@]}"; do
    if [ -n "${repositoryUrl[${mirrorOf[$mirrorId]}]:-}" ]; then
      renames+=(-e "s/maven-metadata-$mirrorId\\.xml/maven-metadata-${mirrorOf[$mirrorId]}.xml/g")
    fi
  done
  local dir name2 remote
  declare -A providedPaths=()
  if [ -f "$work/input-metadata/supplied-paths.json" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r rel; do providedPaths[$rel]=1; done < <(jq -r '.[]' "$work/input-metadata/supplied-paths.json")
  fi
  while IFS= read -r rel; do
    if [ -n "${providedPaths[$rel]:-}" ]; then continue; fi
    dir=$(dirname "$rel")
    name2=$(basename "$rel")
    case $name2 in
    _remote.repositories | *.lastUpdated | *.sha1 | *.md5 | *.sha256 | *.sha512)
      continue
      ;;
    maven-metadata*.xml)
      jq -cn --arg path "$dir/$(sed "${renames[@]}" <<<"$name2")" --rawfile contents "$m2/$rel" \
        '{ path: $path, contents: $contents }' >>"$metadata"
      continue
      ;;
    resolver-status.properties)
      # The resolver checks a version list again a day after the time it
      # records, so the time becomes the year 2100. The comment lines hold
      # the date of the lock run, which a relock would change.
      jq -cn --arg path "$rel" \
        --arg contents "$(sed -E "${renames[@]}" -e '/^#/d' -e 's/=[0-9]{13}$/=4102444800000/' "$m2/$rel")"$'\n' \
        '{ path: $path, contents: $contents }' >>"$metadata"
      continue
      ;;
    esac
    remote=$name2
    id=$(remoteId "$m2/$dir" "$name2")
    # Maven Resolver downloads a SNAPSHOT file under its timestamped name,
    # which it tracks, and keeps an untracked copy under the -SNAPSHOT
    # name. The copy comes from the same URL as the timestamped file the

        if [ -n "$id" ]; then
          remote=$candidate
          break
        fi
      done
    fi
    if [ -z "$id" ]; then
      untracked+=("$rel")
      continue
    fi
    if [ -z "${repositoryUrl[$id]:-}" ]; then
      unknown+=("$rel (repository $id)")
      continue
    fi

    # one repository served it, the repository is the one the mirror

    --argjson version "$PURIFIER_FORMAT" \
    --slurpfile projectInputs "$work/inputs.json" \
    --arg clojureVersion "$(clojureVersion)" \
    --arg javaVersion "$(javaVersion)" \
    --arg projectDir "$projectDir" \
    --argjson definitionFiles "$(printf '%s\n' "${files[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -sc .)" \

    --argjson build "$buildJson" \
    --argjson test "$testJson" \
    --arg group "$group" --arg name "$name" --argjson projectVersion "$version" \
    --argjson pom "$pom" \
    --slurpfile outputs "$outputs" \
    --slurpfile artifacts "$artifacts" \
    --slurpfile metadata "$metadata" \
    --slurpfile git "$gitEntries" \
    --slurpfile gitRepos "$gitRepos" \
    '{
      version: $version,
      clojureVersion: $clojureVersion,
      javaVersion: $javaVersion,
      projectDir: $projectDir,
      definitionFiles: $definitionFiles,
      definitionHash: $definitionHash,
      aliases: $aliases,
      prepared: $prepared,
      userAliases: $userAliases,
      build: $build,
      test: $test,
      project: { group: $group, name: $name, version: $projectVersion },

# `update [LIB...]`: a relock that resolves the version ranges and SNAPSHOTs
# of every library, or of the named ones, anew. A library is named as in
# deps.edn, such as org.clojure/core.memoize.
cmdUpdate() {
  local -a lockArgs=(--force) libs=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
    --lockfile | --mirror | --input)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "update: $1 takes a value"
      lockArgs+=("$1" "$2")
      shift
      ;;
    -*) die "update: unknown argument $1" ;;
    *) libs+=("$1") ;;
    esac
    shift
  done
  if [ ${#libs[@]} = 0 ]; then
    updateAll=1
  else
    local lib group artifact
    for lib in "${libs[@]}"; do
      if [[ $lib == */* ]]; then
        group=${lib%%/*} artifact=${lib#*/}
      else
        group=$lib artifact=$lib
      fi
      updatePrefixes+=("${group//.//}/$artifact/")
    done
  fi
  cmdLock "${lockArgs[@]}"
}

# The state directory of a lockfile: .clojure-cli-purifier beside it. It
# holds the GC root `env`, the writable local repository under `home`, the
# gitlibs directory `gitlibs`, the path of the lockfile in `lockfile`, and
# `bin/clojure`, which runs the Clojure CLI on the locked downloads.
stateOf() {
  echo "$(dirname "$1")/.clojure-cli-purifier"
}

cmdPrefetch() {
  local lockArg=""
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
    --lockfile)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "prefetch: --lockfile takes a path"
      lockArg=$2
      shift
      ;;
    *) die "prefetch: unknown argument $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
  done

  local root lockFile problem
  root=$(projectRoot)
  lockFile=$(lockFileOf "$root" "$lockArg")
  problem=$(lockProblem "$root" "$lockFile")
  [ -z "$problem" ] || die "$problem"

  # nix-build keeps the environment alive with an indirect GC root at
  # state/env.
  local state env
  state=$(stateOf "$lockFile")
  mkdir -p "$state/bin"
  local projectDir
  projectDir=$(lockProjectDir "$lockFile")
  nix-build "$PURIFIER_LIB/realize.nix" --argstr lockFile "$lockFile" \
    --argstr src "$(sourceRootOf "$root" "$projectDir")" --argstr projectDir "$projectDir" \
    --argstr nixpkgs "$PURIFIER_NIXPKGS" --argstr purifierRef "$PURIFIER_SHARED_REF" \
    -o "$state/env" >/dev/null
  env=$(readlink -f "$state/env")

  # The local repository is a writable tree of links into the store, and
  # the gitlibs directory holds writable copies of the checkouts, which a
  # git dependency that needs preparing writes into.
  local home="$state/home" gitlibs="$state/gitlibs"
  chmod -R u+w "$home" "$gitlibs" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf "$home" "$gitlibs" "$state/cache"
  mkdir -p "$home/.m2/repository" "$gitlibs"
  cp -rs --no-preserve=mode "$env/repository/." "$home/.m2/repository"
  # Maven Resolver rewrites the metadata records it reads, so those are
  # writable copies.
  find "$home/.m2/repository" -type l \( -name 'maven-metadata*.xml' -o -name resolver-status.properties \) \
    -exec cp --no-preserve=mode -L {} {}.tmp \; -exec mv {}.tmp {} \;
  cp -rL --no-preserve=mode "$env/gitlibs/." "$gitlibs"
  if [ "$(jq '.projectInputs // [] | length' "$lockFile")" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq '.projectInputs' "$lockFile" > "$state/inputs.json"
    rm -rf "$state/input-metadata"
    python3 "$PURIFIER_PROJECT_INPUTS_TOOLS/project_inputs.py" maven --inputs "$state/inputs.json" \
      --destination "$home/.m2/repository" --metadata "$state/input-metadata" --roots "$state/inputs"
    stageInputAliases "$home/.m2/repository" "$state/input-metadata" \
      "$(sourceRootOf "$root" "$projectDir")" "$gitlibs"
  fi
  echo "$lockFile" >"$state/lockfile"
  jq -r .contentHash "$lockFile" >"$state/prefetched"
  ln -sfn "$(readlink -f "$0")" "$state/bin/clojure"

  # The git dependencies that need preparing are prepared now, as the Nix
  # build prepares them.
  "$state/bin/clojure" -X:deps prep :aliases "[$(jq -r '.prepared | join(" ")' "$lockFile")]" >/dev/null
  echo "clojure-cli-purifier: prefetched $(jq '.artifacts | length' "$lockFile") files and $(jq '.git | length' "$lockFile") git checkouts for $root"
  echo "clojure-cli-purifier: put $state/bin first on PATH, and \`clojure\` runs on them with no network"
}

# `clojure` in the state directory of a lockfile: the Clojure CLI, with the
# prefetched local repository and gitlibs directory in place of those in the
# home directory.
runClojure() {
  local state lockFile root problem
  state=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
  [ -f "$state/lockfile" ] || die "$state holds no prefetch; run clojure-cli-purifier prefetch"
  lockFile=$(cat "$state/lockfile")
  if [ ! -e "$lockFile" ]; then
    echo "clojure-cli-purifier: warning: no clojure-cli-purifier.lock.json found; running clojure impurely. Run \`clojure-cli-purifier lock\` to use Nix-resolved dependencies." >&2
    exec clojure "$@"
  fi
  root=$(projectRoot)
  problem=$(lockProblem "$root" "$lockFile")
  [ -z "$problem" ] || die "$problem"
  [ "$(cat "$state/prefetched")" = "$(jq -r .contentHash "$lockFile")" ] ||
    die "$lockFile changed after the last prefetch; run clojure-cli-purifier prefetch"

  # The JVMs find the local repository through user.home. The Clojure CLI
  # configuration of the user stays in effect. Git trusts the checkouts,
  # which the store owns.
  export GITLIBS="$state/gitlibs"
  export CLJ_CACHE="$state/cache"
  export CLJ_JVM_OPTS="-Duser.home=$state/home ${CLJ_JVM_OPTS:-}"
  export JAVA_OPTS="-Duser.home=$state/home ${JAVA_OPTS:-}"
  export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='*'

  if [ "$(jq '.projectInputs // [] | length' "$lockFile")" -gt 0 ]; then
    export PURIFIER_PROVIDED_CONFIG="$state/input-metadata/project-inputs.edn"
  fi

  # The standard error of the Clojure CLI also goes to a log. When it fails
  # to resolve a download, the lockfile lacks that download.
  local log status=0
  log=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/clojure-cli-purifier-clojure.XXXXXX")
  clojure "$@" 2> >(tee "$log" >&2) || status=$?
  wait
  if [ $status != 0 ] && grep -qE 'could not be resolved|Could not transfer|Could not find artifact|Failed to read artifact descriptor|Unable to clone|Network is unreachable' "$log"; then
    echo "clojure-cli-purifier: the Clojure CLI tried to download something $lockFile does not hold; run clojure-cli-purifier lock, then clojure-cli-purifier prefetch" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
  return $status
}

cmdPublish() {
  local repository="" dryRun=0 lockArg=""
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
    --lockfile)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "publish: --lockfile takes a path"
      lockArg=$2
      shift
      ;;
    --repository)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "publish: --repository takes ID=URL"
      repository=$2
      shift
      ;;
    --dry-run) dryRun=1 ;;
    *) die "publish: unknown argument $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
  done

  local root lockFile problem
  root=$(projectRoot)
  lockFile=$(lockFileOf "$root" "$lockArg")
  problem=$(lockProblem "$root" "$lockFile")
  [ -z "$problem" ] || die "$problem"
  [ "$(jq -r .pom "$lockFile")" != null ] || die "the build of the lock writes no POM, which publishing needs"

  local projectDir release state
  projectDir=$(lockProjectDir "$lockFile")
  state=$(stateOf "$lockFile")
  mkdir -p "$state"
  release=$(nix-build --out-link "$state/release" "$PURIFIER_LIB/release.nix" \
    --argstr nixpkgs "$PURIFIER_NIXPKGS" --argstr purifierRef "$PURIFIER_SHARED_REF" \
    --argstr src "$(sourceRootOf "$root" "$projectDir")" --argstr projectDir "$projectDir" \
    --argstr lockFile "$lockFile")
  [ -n "$PURIFIER_DEPLOY_CLASSPATH" ] || \
    die "this clojure-cli-purifier was built without its deploy tool lockfile"
  "$JAVA_CMD" -cp "$(cat "$PURIFIER_DEPLOY_CLASSPATH")" clojure.main \
    "$PURIFIER_LIB/deploy-projections.clj" "$release/repository" "$release/catalog.json" "$repository" "$dryRun"
}

# Linked as bin/clojure in a state directory, this script is the Clojure
# CLI on the prefetched downloads.
if [ "$(basename "$0")" = clojure ]; then
  runClojure "$@"
  exit
fi

case ${1:-} in
lock)
  shift
  cmdLock "$@"
  ;;
update)
  shift
  cmdUpdate "$@"
  ;;
prefetch)
  shift
  cmdPrefetch "$@"
  ;;
publish)
  shift
  cmdPublish "$@"
  ;;
-h | --help | help)
  usage
  ;;
*)
  usage >&2
  exit 1
  ;;
esac

# Stops unless the lockfile is valid JSON in this command's format and
# the project's build definition is the one it was written for. The
# Nix library checks the content hash when it reads the lockfile.
check_lockfile() {
  [ -f "$lockfile" ] || die "$lockfile does not exist; run cmake-purifier lock first"
  jq -e 'type == "object"' "$lockfile" > /dev/null 2>&1 ||
    die "$lockfile is not valid JSON; restore it from version control, or run cmake-purifier lock to write it again"
  format=$(jq .version "$lockfile")
  [ "$format" = "$lockVersion" ] || die "$lockfile has lock format version $format; this cmake-purifier reads version $lockVersion. Run cmake-purifier lock again."

  current=$(PATH="/nix/store/xgw813vgzl2q0696sq45adpj0xd690jq-git-2.56.0/bin:$PATH" bash "$nixlib/definition-hash.sh" "$source")
  [ "$locked" = "$current" ] ||
    die "$lockfile is older than the project: a CMakeLists.txt or *.cmake file changed since it was written. Run cmake-purifier lock to lock the project again."

prefetch() {

    "{ lockFile }: let pkgs = import $nixpkgs { }; in (pkgs.callPackage $nixlib/sources.nix { inherit lockFile; purifier = import $purifierlib { inherit (pkgs) lib; }; }).tree" \
    --arg lockFile "$lockfile" --out-link "$state/sources-root")

    "$lockedProvider" "$nixlib" "$realGit" "$realHg" "$realSvn" "$realCvs"

    echo 'set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)'

      case "$flag" in
        -D*=*)

          name=${definition%%=*}
          value=${definition#*=}
          type=STRING

            name=${name%%:*}

# Runs a command with mitm-cache replaying the prefetched files as its
# proxy.
replay() {

  [ -e "$state/sources-root" ] || die "$source has no prefetched downloads; run cmake-purifier prefetch first"
  check_lockfile
  tree=$(readlink -f "$state/sources-root")
  ca=$state/ca
  mkdir -p "$ca"
  [ -f "$ca/ca.cer" ] || {
    openssl genrsa -out "$ca/ca.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
    openssl req -x509 -new -nodes -key "$ca/ca.key" -sha256 -days 3650 -out "$ca/ca.cer" -subj "/CN=cmake-purifier" 2>/dev/null
  }
  port=$(ephemeral-port-reserve 127.0.0.1)
  mitm-cache -l "127.0.0.1:$port" -k "$ca/ca.key" -c "$ca/ca.cer" replay "$tree/http" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  replayer=$!
  trap 'kill "$replayer" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
  await_port "$port"
  status=0
  ( proxy_env "$port" "$ca/ca.cer"; "${args[@]}" ) || status=$?
  exit "$status"
}

publish() {
  [ ${#args[@]} -eq 2 ] || usage
  tag=${args[0]}
  release=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "${args[1]}")
  files=()
  for file in "$release"/*; do
    [ -f "$file" ] && files+=("$file")
  done
  [ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ] || die "${args[1]} built $release, which holds no files to upload"
  repoArgs=()
  [ -z "$repo" ] || repoArgs=(--repo "$repo")

  ghCommand=$(command -v gh || echo /nix/store/ri8q81g024g6zkmljbnr6wylw8zs5c92-gh-2.103.3/bin/gh)
  "$ghCommand" release upload "$tag" "${files[@]}" --clobber ${repoArgs[@]+"${repoArgs[@]}"}
  echo "cmake-purifier: uploaded ${#files[@]} files to the release $tag" >&2
}

# Relocks with the configure arguments of the lockfile, moving the
# checkouts of the named dependencies or repositories, or of every one.
update() {
  [ -f "$lockfile" ] || die "$lockfile does not exist; run cmake-purifier lock first"
  jq -e --argjson version "$lockVersion" '.version == $version' "$lockfile" > /dev/null 2>&1 ||
    die "$lockfile is not a cmake-purifier lockfile of version $lockVersion; run cmake-purifier lock to write it again"
  updateNames=(${args[@]+"${args[@]}"})
  if [ ${#updateNames[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    updateAll=true
  fi
  for name in ${updateNames[@]+"${updateNames[@]}"}; do
    jq -e --arg name "$name" '
      [.dependencies[].name, (.gitCheckouts[].url), ((.hgCheckouts // [])[].repo),
       ((.svnCheckouts // [])[].repo), ((.cvsCheckouts // [])[].repo)] | index($name)' "$lockfile" > /dev/null ||
      die "$lockfile has no dependency or repository named $name"
  done
  mapfile -t args < <(jq -r '.cmakeFlags[]' "$lockfile")
  lock
}

case "$command" in
  lock) lock ;;
  update) update ;;
  prefetch) prefetch ;;
  replay) replay ;;
  publish) publish ;;
  *) usage ;;
esac

#
# The gradle-purifier command. pkgs/gradle-purifier substitutes the @…@
# names and runs it as a writeShellApplication, which sets errexit,
# nounset and pipefail.
#
#   gradle-purifier lock [--relock] [--java <major>] [--lockfile <path>] [-- <gradle arguments>]
#       records every download of the build in the lockfile
#   gradle-purifier update [--java <major>] [--lockfile <path>] [<group>:<artifact>...] [-- <gradle arguments>]
#       moves dynamic versions, and Gradle's own lockfiles, to the newest
#       versions, then records the downloads as lock does
#   gradle-purifier prefetch [--lockfile <path>]
#       realizes the locked downloads, the JDK, the Gradle distribution and
#       the Kotlin/Native toolchain, and installs the init script that makes
#       ./gradlew, a Gradle on the PATH and an IDE read them, offline
#   gradle-purifier publish [--lockfile <path>] [<gradle arguments>]
#       publishes what Nix built from the lockfile, through the build's
#       own publish tasks
#
# Each command runs at the root of a Gradle build. The lockfile is
# gradle-purifier.lock.json there, or the path that --lockfile or
# GRADLE_PURIFIER_LOCKFILE names, for a build kept external. The GC roots
# lie beside the lockfile, in .gradle-purifier.

# A failure inside $(…) stops the command too.
shopt -s inherit_errexit

lib=/nix/store/psnk9zls9yc8mj0j5sygwr1p379wld7r-lib
recorder=/nix/store/sal5mpcjv2j1jzxvzds5b2006grkd7q6-gradle-purifier-recorder
default_java=/nix/store/8av96xmb7arqavl2n3nwskrhk5q31h85-openjdk-headless-21.0.12.1+1/lib/openjdk
lock_version=1
# The nixpkgs and the nix-purifiers library the command builds with.
sdk_descriptor=/nix/store/cdr6fb2gqsbc8i1abbycq4cbp0v9vsb4-gradle-sdk-source.json
nixpkgs=/nix/store/10zfgh0n1xj6r62r4xbsjf9z71mcwril-cm5m4hjjh37s6z82rwa0vhkbcga3m8bq-source
purifier_source=/nix/store/75wc7321969zfq7ybs5mr61bxl6271j7-source
# The dynamic linker the programs Kotlin/Native links name, from that
# package set.
dynamic_linker=/nix/store/pqyiidz5mi73wv5f91d48s9plcqyj5bz-glibc-2.44-57/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2

portal=https/plugins.gradle.org/m2
# The hosts Kotlin/Native downloads its toolchain from: its
# dependenciesUrl, and the CDN that redirects to.
konan_hosts=(download.jetbrains.com download-cdn.jetbrains.com)

die() {
  echo "gradle-purifier: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  gradle-purifier lock [--relock] [--java <major>] [--lockfile <path>] [-- <gradle arguments>]
      Records every file the build downloads, by URL and hash, and the
      outputs of every project, in gradle-purifier.lock.json. The lock is
      made again only when the build definition changed, unless --relock
      is given. Gradle runs on nixpkgs' JDK of the major version --java
      names, or of the Java the lockfile was made with; a first lock runs
      on JAVA_HOME, or on the command's JDK 21. The gradle
      arguments are recorded and passed to every Gradle run of the lock.
      A dynamic version, such as 3.17.+, resolves as it did in the lock
      before, from the version listings the lockfile holds.
  gradle-purifier update [--java <major>] [--lockfile <path>] [<group>:<artifact>...] [-- <gradle arguments>]
      Locks again with the newest versions that the dynamic versions of
      the build allow: of every package, or of the packages named
      (group:* names every artifact of a group). In a build with Gradle's
      dependency locking, it runs Gradle with --write-locks, or with
      --update-locks for the packages named, and writes the Gradle
      lockfiles back into the build. It keeps the gradle arguments of the
      lock unless it is given others.
  gradle-purifier prefetch [--lockfile <path>]
      Realizes in the Nix store everything the development loop and an IDE
      need: the locked downloads, the JDK, the Gradle distribution (where
      ./gradlew looks for it) and a Kotlin/Native toolchain. It installs an
      init script in the init.d of the Gradle user home that makes the
      builds of this root read them, so ./gradlew build, a Gradle on the
      PATH and an IDE work with the network cut off. Run it after each
      lock.
  gradle-purifier publish [--lockfile <path>] [<gradle arguments>]
      Builds the release with Nix from the lockfile, and runs the build's
      publish tasks (publish, unless gradle arguments name others) with the
      files Nix built in place of the ones Gradle would make.

The lockfile is gradle-purifier.lock.json at the build root, or the path
--lockfile or GRADLE_PURIFIER_LOCKFILE names.
EOF
}

# The build root, the lockfile and the directory of GC roots, set by
# set_paths.
root=
lockfile=
state=

# Sets root, lockfile and state, from the --lockfile argument $1 (or "").
set_paths() {
  if [ ! -f settings.gradle ] && [ ! -f settings.gradle.kts ]; then
    die "run this at the root of a Gradle build (the directory with settings.gradle or settings.gradle.kts)"
  fi
  root=$PWD
  local given=${1:-${GRADLE_PURIFIER_LOCKFILE:-}}
  if [ -n "$given" ]; then
    lockfile=$(realpath -m -- "$given")
  else
    lockfile=$root/gradle-purifier.lock.json
  fi
  state=$(dirname "$lockfile")/.gradle-purifier
}

# The home of the JDK at the store path $1: lib/openjdk in nixpkgs'
# OpenJDK on Linux, the store path itself in its Zulu JDK on Darwin.
jdk_home() {
  if [ -d "$1/lib/openjdk" ]; then
    printf '%s/lib/openjdk' "$1"
  else
    printf '%s' "$1"
  fi
}

# The home of nixpkgs' headless JDK of the major version $1, built with
# Nix (GC root in the state directory).
nixpkgs_jdk() {
  local out
  mkdir -p "$state"
  out=$(nix-build --quiet --out-link "$state/jdk-$1" "$nixpkgs" \
    -A "javaPackages.compiler.openjdk$1.headless") || die "nixpkgs has no headless OpenJDK $1"
  jdk_home "$out"
}

# The JDK to run the lock on: nixpkgs' JDK of the major version $1 when it
# is given; otherwise JAVA_HOME when it is set, and the command's own JDK
# when it is not.
java_home() {
  if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
    nixpkgs_jdk "$1"
  elif [ -n "${JAVA_HOME:-}" ]; then
    echo "$JAVA_HOME"
  else
    echo "$default_java"
  fi
}

# The distribution URL of the wrapper properties, with the escapes of the
# properties format removed.
distribution_url() {
  local properties=gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
  [ -f "$properties" ] || die "the build has no $properties; add a wrapper with 'gradle wrapper'"
  local url
  url=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*distributionUrl[[:space:]]*[=:][[:space:]]*//p' "$properties" | tail -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
  [ -n "$url" ] || die "$properties sets no distributionUrl"
  printf '%s' "${url//\\/}"
}

# The path of a URL in the tree of locked downloads.
tree_path() {
  local url=$1
  local scheme=${url%%://*}
  printf '%s/%s' "$scheme" "${url#*://}"
}

# The hash of the build definition at the build root with the gradle
# arguments of the JSON list $1, as nix/lib/inputs.nix computes it; the
# builder computes it the same way.
# Source mode has a separate pure command path. The original entry points
# retain their argument and identity meanings for undeclared projects.
source_sdk_mode() {
  [ -f "$root/gradle-purifier.sdks.json" ] || {
    [ -f "$lockfile" ] && jq -e '[.projectJdks // {} | .[] | .version == "jvm-sdk-context-v2"] | any' "$lockfile" >/dev/null 2>&1
  }
}

sdk_source_command() {
  python3 "$lib/project-sdk-sources.py" "$@" --helper "$purifier_source" --nixpkgs "$nixpkgs"
}

pure_project_snapshot() {
  mkdir -p "$state"
  copy_build "$state/pure-project"
}

selected_java_home() {
  if source_sdk_mode; then
    jq -er '.launchHome' "$sdk_context"
  else
    jdk_home "$1"
  fi
}

inputs_hash() {
  if source_sdk_mode; then
    pure_project_snapshot
    sdk_source_command hash --project "$state/pure-project" --arguments "$1"
    return
  fi
  nix-instantiate --eval --strict --json \
    --expr "{ src, args }: import $lib/inputs.nix { lib = (import $nixpkgs { }).lib; src = /. + src; gradleArguments = builtins.fromJSON args; }" \
    --argstr src "$root" --argstr args "$1" | jq -r .
}

# The contentHash of the lockfile $1: SHA-256 of its JSON without
# contentHash, with sorted keys and no spaces, as builtins.toJSON writes
# it; read-lock.nix checks it.
content_hash() {
  printf 'sha256:%s' "$(jq -j -S -c 'del(.contentHash)' "$1" | sha256sum | cut -d ' ' -f 1)"
}

# Unpacks the Gradle distribution zip $1 into the user's cache, once, and
# prints its Gradle home.
unpack_distribution() {
  local zip=$1
  local cache=${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/gradle-purifier/distributions
  local name
  name=$(basename "$(readlink -f "$zip")")
  local dir=$cache/$name
  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$cache"
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp -d "$cache/.unpack.XXXXXX")
    unzip -q "$zip" -d "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$dir"
  fi
  local home
  home=$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | head -n 1)
  [ -x "$home/bin/gradle" ] || die "$zip holds no bin/gradle"
  printf '%s' "$home"
}

# Copies the build at the current directory to $1, leaving out version
# control, Gradle's state, IDE files and the build directory of every
# project.
copy_build() {
  local target=$1
  local excludes=(--exclude=/.git --exclude=.gradle --exclude=.gradle-purifier --exclude=.kotlin --exclude=.idea --exclude=/result*)
  local script dir
  while IFS= read -r script; do
    dir=$(dirname "${script#./}")
    if [ "$dir" = . ]; then excludes+=(--exclude=/build/); else excludes+=(--exclude="/$dir/build/"); fi
  done < <(find . \( -name .git -o -name .gradle -o -name build -o -name node_modules \) -prune -o \
    -type f \( -name 'build.gradle' -o -name 'build.gradle.kts' -o -name 'settings.gradle' -o -name 'settings.gradle.kts' \) -print)
  mkdir -p "$target"
  rsync -a --delete "${excludes[@]}" ./ "$target/"
}

# Kotlin/Native downloads its toolchain (LLVM, a GCC toolchain with a
# sysroot, and more) with its own downloader, and deletes each archive
# once it has extracted it. The downloader names every download in the
# build's output, as "Downloading dependency <url> to <file>". Records
# each such URL from the Gradle output $1 as a download into the records
# file $2, fetching it into the store for its hash.
record_konan_dependencies() {
  local log=$1 records=$2
  local url hash
  while IFS= read -r url; do
    echo "gradle-purifier: fetching $url" >&2
    hash=$(nix --extra-experimental-features nix-command store prefetch-file --json --hash-type sha256 "$url" | jq -r '.hash')
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(tree_path "$url")" "$url" "$hash" >>"$records"
  done < <(konan_download_urls "$log")
}

# The URLs Kotlin/Native's downloader names in the Gradle output $1, each
# once.
konan_download_urls() {
  sed -n 's/^Downloading dependency \(https\?:\/\/[^ ]*\) to .*/\1/p' "$1" | sort -u
}

# The lockfile's artifacts, as JSON, from the recorder's records file $1:
# a file entry { url, hash } for each line with a URL, and an inline entry
# { path, contents } for each line the recorder marked "inline" (its third
# field is the contents in Base64); one entry per path, in the order of
# the paths. Nix derives the path and the mirrors of a file entry from its
# URL.
artifacts_json() {
  jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t"))
    | sort_by(.[0], (if .[1] == "inline" then 0 else 1 end))
    | unique_by(.[0])
    | map(if .[1] == "inline" then {path: .[0], contents: (.[2] | @base64d)}
          else {url: .[1], hash: .[2]} end)' "$1"
}

# The Kotlin/Native name of this machine. A Kotlin/Native toolchain runs
# on the machine it was made for, so the lock records it.
konan_host() {
  case $(uname -m) in
    x86_64) echo linux_x64 ;;
    aarch64 | arm64) echo linux_arm64 ;;
    *) uname -m ;;
  esac
}

# The konanHost of the lockfile, as JSON: the Kotlin/Native name of this
# machine when the records file $1 holds a download of a Kotlin/Native
# toolchain, and null otherwise, so that the lock of a build without
# Kotlin/Native is the same on every machine.
lock_konan_host() {
  if grep -q -F 'https://download.jetbrains.com/kotlin/native/' "$1"; then
    printf '"%s"' "$(konan_host)"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}

lock_command() {
  local relock='' java_major='' given='' input_args=() refresh_inputs=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
      --relock) relock=1; shift ;;
      --input)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--input takes a flake package"
        input_args+=(--input "$2")
        relock=1
        shift 2
        ;;
      --java)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--java takes a Java major version, such as 17"
        java_major=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
      --lockfile)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--lockfile takes a path"
        given=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
      --) shift; break ;;
      -h | --help) usage; exit 0 ;;
      *) die "lock takes --relock, --java <major>, --lockfile <path> and, after --, gradle arguments; got $1" ;;
    esac
  done
  local gradle_args=("$@")
  set_paths "$given"

  local args_json current
  args_json=$(jq -n -c '$ARGS.positional' --args -- "${gradle_args[@]}")
  if [ -f "$root/gradle-purifier.sdks.json" ] && [ -n "$java_major" ]; then
    die "--java cannot be combined with gradle-purifier.sdks.json; select the manager in the declaration"
  fi
  current=$(inputs_hash "$args_json")
  if [ -z "$relock" ] && [ -f "$lockfile" ] \
    && jq -e --argjson version "$lock_version" --arg current "$current" \
      '.version == $version and .inputsHash == $current' "$lockfile" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && [ "$(jq -r '.contentHash' "$lockfile")" = "$(content_hash "$lockfile")" ]; then
    echo "gradle-purifier: $lockfile is current" >&2
    return 0
  fi

  mkdir -p "$state"
  pinned_listings >"$state/pinned.tsv"
  update_args=()
  run_lock "$(lock_java "$java_major")" "$state/pinned.tsv" '' "${gradle_args[@]}"
}

update_command() {
  local java_major='' given='' have_args='' packages=() gradle_args=() input_args=() refresh_inputs=()
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
      --input)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--input takes a flake package"
        input_args+=(--input "$2")
        shift 2
        ;;
      --java)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--java takes a Java major version, such as 17"
        java_major=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
      --lockfile)
        [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--lockfile takes a path"
        given=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
      --)
        shift
        gradle_args=("$@")
        have_args=1
        break
        ;;
      -h | --help) usage; exit 0 ;;
      -*) die "update takes --java <major>, --lockfile <path>, packages and, after --, gradle arguments; got $1" ;;
      *)
        [[ $1 == *:* ]] || die "a package is group:artifact, or group:* for every artifact of a group; got $1"
        packages+=("$1")
        shift
        ;;
    esac
  done
  set_paths "$given"
  # The update keeps the gradle arguments of the lock unless it is given
  # others.
  if [ -z "$have_args" ] && [ -f "$lockfile" ]; then
    mapfile -t gradle_args < <(jq -r '.gradleArguments[]?' "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi

  mkdir -p "$state"
  : >"$state/pinned.tsv"
  update_args=()
  if [ -f "$root/gradle-purifier.sdks.json" ] && [ -n "$java_major" ]; then
    die "--java cannot be combined with gradle-purifier.sdks.json; select the manager in the declaration"
  fi
  if [ ${#packages[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    pinned_listings "${packages[@]}" >"$state/pinned.tsv"
    if uses_dependency_locking; then
      update_args=(--update-locks "$(IFS=,; echo "${packages[*]}")")
    fi
  elif uses_dependency_locking; then
    update_args=(--write-locks)
  fi
  if [ ${#packages[@]} = 0 ]; then refresh_inputs=(--refresh); resource_refresh=1; fi
  run_lock "$(lock_java "$java_major")" "$state/pinned.tsv" 1 "${gradle_args[@]}"
}

# The Java major version a lock runs on: $1 when --java gave one, else the
# one of the existing lockfile, so that a relock keeps the Java of the
# lock it replaces; empty for a first lock, which runs on JAVA_HOME or the
# JDK of the command.
lock_java() {
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    echo "$1"
  elif [ -f "$lockfile" ]; then
    jq -r '.javaMajor // empty' "$lockfile" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

# The version listings (maven-metadata files) of the lockfile, for the
# recorder to serve in place of the remote ones (GRADLE_PURIFIER_PINNED):
# a line of the path and the contents in Base64 for each listing, except
# the listings of the packages $@ (group:artifact, or group:* for every
# artifact of a group). A lockfile of another format version pins
# nothing, and a lockfile that is not JSON fails the command.
pinned_listings() {
  [ -f "$lockfile" ] || return 0
  jq -r --argjson version "$lock_version" --args '
    ($ARGS.positional | map(split(":") | {group: (.[0] | gsub("\\."; "/")), artifact: (.[1] // "*")})) as $updated
    | select(.version == $version)
    | .artifacts[]
    | select(.contents != null)
    | (.path | split("/")) as $segments
    | select(($segments | length) > 2)
    | select(
        ($segments[-2]) as $artifact
        | ($segments[:-2] | join("/")) as $groupDir
        | $updated
        | any(. as $u | ($groupDir | endswith("/" + $u.group)) and ($u.artifact == "*" or $u.artifact == $artifact))
        | not)
    | [.path, (.contents | @base64)]
    | @tsv' "$@" <"$lockfile" || die "$lockfile is not JSON; restore it from version control, or delete it and run 'gradle-purifier lock'"
}

# Whether the build uses Gradle's dependency locking: Gradle wrote a
# lockfile somewhere in it.
uses_dependency_locking() {
  [ -n "$(find . \( -name .git -o -name .gradle -o -name .gradle-purifier -o -name build -o -name node_modules \) -prune -o \
    -type f -name '*gradle.lockfile' -print -quit)" ]
}

# The gradle arguments of an update that writes Gradle's own lockfiles,
# which the lock does not record.
update_args=()

# The lock run: Gradle on the JDK of the Java major version $1 (or the
# default), with the recorder serving the pinned version listings of the
# file $2; when $3 is not empty, Gradle's own lockfiles are copied back
# from the lock run to the build. The gradle arguments follow.
run_lock() {
  local java_major=$1 pins=$2 copy_back=$3
  shift 3
  local gradle_args=("$@")
  local args_json
  args_json=$(jq -n -c '$ARGS.positional' --args -- "${gradle_args[@]}")

  local url
  url=$(distribution_url)
  echo "gradle-purifier: fetching $url" >&2
  local prefetch dist_hash dist_zip
  prefetch=$(nix --extra-experimental-features nix-command store prefetch-file --json --hash-type sha256 "$url")
  dist_hash=$(jq -r '.hash' <<<"$prefetch")
  dist_zip=$(jq -r '.storePath' <<<"$prefetch")
  local gradle_home
  gradle_home=$(unpack_distribution "$dist_zip")

  local work=$state/lock-run
  rm -rf "$work"
  mkdir -p "$work"
  copy_build "$work/build"
  local previous_args=()
  if [ -f "$lockfile" ]; then previous_args=(--previous "$lockfile"); fi
  python3 "$purifier_source/tools/project_inputs.py" pin "${previous_args[@]}" \
    "${input_args[@]}" "${refresh_inputs[@]}" --output "$work/inputs.json"
  if [ "$(jq length "$work/inputs.json")" -gt 0 ]; then
    python3 "$purifier_source/tools/project_inputs.py" maven --inputs "$work/inputs.json" \
      --destination "$work/provided" --metadata "$work/input-metadata" --roots "$work/inputs"
    export GRADLE_PURIFIER_PROVIDED_REPOSITORY="$work/provided"
    export GRADLE_PURIFIER_PROVIDED_CATALOG="$work/input-metadata/catalog.json"
  fi

  local records=$work/records.tsv
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(tree_path "$url")" "$url" "$dist_hash" >"$records"
  local java
  local source_context='' source_capture_args=() source_environment=() source_native_args=()
  if [ -f "$root/gradle-purifier.sdks.json" ]; then
    source_context=$(sdk_source_command preflight --declaration "$root/gradle-purifier.sdks.json" --root "$state/project-sdk-source-context")
    java=$(jq -er '.launchHome' "$source_context")
    source_capture_args=(--source-context "$source_context")
    source_environment=("GRADLE_PURIFIER_JDK_CONTEXT=$source_context")
    local discovery_configuration
    discovery_configuration=$("$default_java/bin/java" "$lib/SdkDiscoveryProperties.java" "$root/gradle.properties" "$work/gradle-home/gradle.properties" -- "${gradle_args[@]}")
    if [ "$discovery_configuration" = absent ]; then
      source_native_args=("-Porg.gradle.java.installations.paths=$(jq -r '.paths | join(",")' "$source_context")" -Porg.gradle.java.installations.auto-detect=false)
    fi
  else
    java=$(java_home "$java_major")
  fi
  # Empty jdk.http.auth.*.disabledSchemes let the recorder send the Basic
  # credentials of an https_proxy URL to the proxy, for HTTPS tunnels and
  # for plain HTTP alike.
  # The recorder is a purifier process with Java 17 bytecode/APIs. Keep it
  # on the bundled runtime while Gradle uses the project-selected JDK below.
  GRADLE_PURIFIER_PINNED=$pins \
    "$default_java/bin/java" -Djdk.http.auth.tunneling.disabledSchemes= -Djdk.http.auth.proxying.disabledSchemes= \
    -cp "$recorder" Recorder "$records" "$work/port" "${konan_hosts[@]}" &
  local recorder_pid=$!
  # shellcheck disable=SC2064 # the PID is known now
  trap "kill $recorder_pid 2>/dev/null || true" EXIT
  local waited=0
  while [ ! -f "$work/port" ]; do
    kill -0 "$recorder_pid" 2>/dev/null || die "the recorder did not start"
    [ $waited -lt 300 ] || die "the recorder did not start within 30 seconds"
    sleep 0.1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
  done
  local ports base tunnel_port
  read -r -a ports <"$work/port" || true
  base=http://127.0.0.1:${ports[0]}
  tunnel_port=${ports[1]}

  local gradle_flags=()
  GRADLE_PURIFIER_MODE='' JAVA_HOME=$java GRADLE_USER_HOME=$work/gradle-home \
    python3 "$lib/gradle-flags.py" capture "$work/gradle-help.txt" --gradle "$gradle_home/bin/gradle" --arguments-json "$args_json" >"$work/gradle-flags.txt" \
    || die "could not select native Gradle controls"
  mapfile -t gradle_flags <"$work/gradle-flags.txt"

  # Read the unpacked native distribution's version, not its URL's filename.
  GRADLE_PURIFIER_MODE='' JAVA_HOME=$java GRADLE_USER_HOME=$work/gradle-home \
    "$gradle_home/bin/gradle" --version >"$work/gradle-version.txt" \
    || die "could not read the native Gradle version"
  local native_gradle_version
  native_gradle_version=$(sed -n 's/^Gradle //p' "$work/gradle-version.txt")
  [[ $native_gradle_version =~ ^[0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+_-]*$ ]] \
    || die "the native distribution did not return one recognizable Gradle version"

  echo "gradle-purifier: running the lock build in $work/build" >&2
  local legacy_bindings='[]' legacy_metadata_capture=0
  if [ -f "$lockfile" ]; then
    legacy_bindings=$(jq -c '[.projects[] | .path as $path | .publications[] | select(.kind == "legacy-maven-upload") | {path:$path,publication:.}]' "$lockfile") \
      || die "could not read existing legacy publication bindings"
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$lockfile" ] || [ "${relock:-}" = 1 ]; then
    legacy_metadata_capture=1
  fi
  if [ "$native_gradle_version" = 5.6.4 ]; then
    # readLock identifies this exact basic profile from the locked distribution.
    # A renamed archive must not give the builder a different profile identity.
    [ "${url##*/}" = gradle-5.6.4-bin.zip ] \
      || die "the native Gradle5.6.4 basic profile requires its matching gradle-5.6.4-bin.zip distribution identity"
    legacy_metadata_capture=0
  fi
  if ! (
    cd "$work/build" || exit 1
    # Gradle's own HTTP client reaches only the recorder: a remote it
    # contacts directly goes to a proxy that refuses, so a download the
    # lock would miss fails here rather than in the sandbox. The HTTPS
    # proxy is the recorder's tunnel, which reaches Kotlin/Native's
    # download host and refuses every other.
    env "${source_environment[@]}" \
      "KONAN_DATA_DIR=$work/konan" \
      "GRADLE_USER_HOME=$work/gradle-home" \
      GRADLE_PURIFIER_MODE=lock \
      "GRADLE_PURIFIER_LEGACY_PUBLICATIONS=$legacy_bindings" \
      "GRADLE_PURIFIER_LEGACY_METADATA_CAPTURE=$legacy_metadata_capture" \
      "GRADLE_PURIFIER_BUILD_ROOT=$work/build" \

import functools, hashlib, http.server, json, pathlib, threading, urllib.request
root = pathlib.Path('/nix/store/byaqady9jj7gxw1jmg3nd37jcy6x8drl-resource-projection')
catalog = json.loads((root / 'catalog.json').read_text())
assert catalog['files']
handler = functools.partial(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler,
                            directory='/nix/store/byaqady9jj7gxw1jmg3nd37jcy6x8drl-resource-projection/files')
with http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), handler) as server:
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    try:
        base = 'http://127.0.0.1:' + str(server.server_port)
        with open('resources.txt', 'w') as expected:
            for name, record in sorted(catalog['files'].items()):
                contents = urllib.request.urlopen(base + '/' + urllib.parse.quote(name)).read()
                assert hashlib.sha256(contents).hexdigest() == record['sha256']
                expected.write(name + '\t' + record['sha256'] + '\n')
        for hidden in ('catalog.json', 'nix-support/inputs'):
            if hidden not in catalog['files']:
                try:
                    urllib.request.urlopen(base + '/' + hidden)
                    raise AssertionError('served metadata: ' + hidden)
                except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
                    assert error.code == 404
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        thread.join()

import java.security.MessageDigest;

public class Resources {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    for (String line : Files.readAllLines(Path.of("resources.txt"))) {
      String[] parts = line.split("\t", 2);
      try (var stream = Resources.class.getResourceAsStream("/" + parts[0])) {
        if (stream == null) throw new AssertionError(parts[0]);
        String digest = HexFormat.of().formatHex(MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(stream.readAllBytes()));
        if (!digest.equals(parts[1])) throw new AssertionError(parts[0]);
      }
    }
  }
}
